what: Cohen kappa on the 56 held-out maintainer-labelled clusters, one entry per full re-triage of that half. Provider routing differs between runs because the free tiers meter per model per minute, and that is most of the spread.
reading: Every 1.2 run scores above every 1.1 run, so the rubric change is doing something. The size of it is not pinned down: 1.2 spans 0.604 to 0.764 across three runs, so a single published figure carries roughly that much slack. The number quoted elsewhere is the one belonging to the corpus you can download, not the best of the three.

bgl_line_metric_across_runs.what: Line-level noise suppression on the 80,000-line BGL slice, one entry per full re-triage. The spread is not the pipeline changing; it is one cluster changing.
bgl_line_metric_across_runs.why: The cluster 'generating <*>' is 65,454 of the 80,000 lines, and its content is 'RAS KERNEL INFO generating core.304' - a core dump. Read as text that is a crash; read by the people who ran the machine it is routine, and they labelled all 65,454 lines '-'. The model has landed on both sides across runs, and because the cluster is 76% of the corpus the line metric follows it.

why_1.2_was_rejected.what: Measured 2026-09-29 on the corpus as it was then (80,000-line BGL slice). 1.2 won its held-out half and cost these elsewhere.
